detail.reinstallDockerMessage: This runs Docker's official installer, which pulls the current engine — on an up-to-date server that is a major upgrade. Installing or upgrading Docker restarts the daemon, and that restarts every container on this server, including anything Openship is running here. Nothing else installs Docker for you: other steps skip it while it is working.

banner.unreachableBody: Openship couldn't open an SSH connection to {host}:{port}. Make sure the server is running and that sshd is accepting connections on port {port}. If it's behind a firewall or NAT, confirm the host is reachable from this machine.
banner.authBody: Reached {host}:{port} but the server refused authentication. The key or password stored for this server doesn't match what's authorised in ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the host.
banner.noServerBody: This server entry is missing SSH settings. Open Edit to set the host, user and credentials, then run a health check.
banner.hostChannelTitle: Openship can't reach this machine's host
banner.hostChannelBody: Openship runs in a container here and talks to the host over SSH at {target}. Nothing answered there, so it can't run host-level operations on this box.
banner.hostChannelImpact: Ordinary deploys to this box still work — they go through the Docker socket. Blocked until the channel works: the host terminal, host system info and host port scans; taking over :80/:443 from a proxy Openship didn't start; installing or updating the mail engine; deploying a catalog app that needs a generated config file on the host (Supabase's kong.yml, say). This box also reads "Offline" in the dashboard's server list while the channel is down.
banner.hostChannelFix: Run this on the host, then retry:
banner.hostChannelMissingTitle: Openship has no channel to this machine's host
banner.hostChannelMissingBody: Openship runs in a container here, and the SSH channel it uses to reach the host was never provisioned. There was no address to contact, so nothing here is down — host-level operations on this box just have nowhere to run.
banner.hostChannelWouldUse: Once provisioned the channel will reach the host at {target}. Nothing has contacted that address yet.
banner.hostChannelProvisionFix: Run this on the host to provision the channel, then retry:
banner.hostChannelAuthBody: Openship runs in a container here and reaches the host over SSH at {target}. The host answered and then rejected the key, so host-level operations can't run. Either the key is no longer authorised for that account, or sshd doesn't permit that account to log in at all. The SSH credentials stored on this server are not used for this connection — the channel has its own key.
banner.hostChannelReauthorizeFix: Run this on the host to re-authorize the channel key, then retry:
banner.unknownBody: Openship couldn't talk to this server.
banner.checkPowered: Is the VPS / VM powered on?
banner.pingSuffix: from this machine - does it answer?

managed.title: Managed private network
managed.description: OpenShip creates an encrypted WireGuard network between your servers, including servers at different providers.
managed.requirements: Requires Linux with systemd and root or passwordless sudo. Missing Python 3.8+, iproute2 and WireGuard tools are installed automatically. Kernel and firewall compatibility are checked during setup.
managed.existingHint: Use addresses already configured on your provider network.
managed.endpointHint: Leave empty to use the server’s SSH address. Each server must be reachable by the other servers over UDP; use a forwarded port when behind NAT.
managed.rangeHint: OpenShip checks host, Docker, VPN, DNS and route ranges, then allocates stable private addresses. You can also choose a private /16–/27 subnet.
managed.effect: Creates a dedicated tunnel and private routes, and allows traffic between the listed peers. SSH routes and DNS settings stay as they are.
managed.keys: Private keys are generated and kept on each server.
managed.rollbackHint: Uncommitted changes roll back on each host after 20 minutes, including after a controller disconnect or host reboot.
managed.firewallHint: OpenShip configures supported host firewalls during Apply. Save provider or router rules before applying or retrying.
managed.expired: This plan expired. Go back and inspect the servers again.
managed.rotateHint: Replace the keys on all members as part of this reviewed change.
managed.recoveryHint: Check the server results before resuming. OpenShip inspects host receipts and restores or reapplies the approved configuration.
managed.removalHint: Remove the managed tunnel, private routes and owned firewall rules from every member. Services using these private addresses will lose their connections.
managed.preparationDescription: Check requirements and install missing tools before reviewing your network.
managed.preparationHint: Preparation installs missing tools. Tunnel, route and firewall changes start after you review and apply the network plan.
managed.progressSaved: Progress is saved. You can leave this page and return from Servers.
managed.liveReconnecting: Connection interrupted. Reconnecting to saved progress…
managed.liveDisconnected: Live updates disconnected. Your progress is saved.
managed.retryPreparationHint: Retry checks every server again and installs only missing tools. Completed installations are reused.
managed.discardDescription: Remove this unfinished setup from your networks. Existing servers, services and installed tools are kept.
managed.cleanupDescription: Remove the network changes made by this attempt from every server, then remove the unfinished network. Servers and services are kept. If a server is unreachable, cleanup stays open so you can retry.
managed.restoreDescription: Restore the network configuration from before this operation. The existing network stays in place and can be removed afterward from its page. If a server is unreachable, recovery stays open.
managed.setupCleanedHint: The network changes were cleaned up and the unfinished network was removed. Your servers are available to use again.
managed.setupDiscardedHint: This setup was discarded. Installed tools are kept; a new setup will reuse them.
managed.cleanupBeforeRemove: This network has unfinished network changes. Restore or clean up the current operation before removing it.
managed.removeSetupServerDescription: Save the remaining {count} servers and pause setup until you press Retry preparation. The server, its services, data, and installed tools stay in place.
managed.removeSetupServerResetDescription: Restore this attempt’s OpenShip network changes on the selected server and its peers, then pause with the remaining {count} servers. Press Retry preparation when you are ready. Services, data, and installed tools stay in place. Every server must acknowledge cleanup before retrying preparation.
managed.keepTwoServers: At least two servers must remain.
managed.resetBeforeContinueDescription: OpenShip restores this attempt’s network configuration and peer entries. After every server confirms cleanup, press Retry preparation to continue with {count} servers. If a server is unreachable, restore access and retry cleanup.
managed.selectionSavedHint: Your updated server selection is saved. Preparation stays paused until you press Retry preparation.
managed.selectionReplacedHint: This attempt is linked to an updated server selection. Open the updated setup to continue.
managed.transportCheckHint: After you apply, OpenShip tests encrypted connections on these UDP endpoints before assigning private addresses and routes.
managed.transportFailedTitle: Check the failed connections before retrying
managed.transportFailedHint: An encrypted connection could not be established. Confirm the destination addresses and any NAT port forwarding, then check firewall rules. Select a failed link to see each direction.
managed.preparationTopologyHint: Each server shows its current preparation step. UDP connectivity is tested after you review and apply the network.
managed.installationTopologyHint: Select a server to open its setup steps, or a connection to inspect its checks.

firewallRules.title: Firewall rules
firewallRules.description: Add these rules to each server’s provider firewall or upstream router. Outbound rules are needed only when outgoing traffic is restricted.
firewallRules.copyFailed: Copy is unavailable here. Select and copy the displayed values.
firewallRules.pending: Rules fill in when preparation resolves every server’s transport IPv4 and port. If preparation fails, resolve the reported errors before copying the complete template.
firewallRules.scopeHint: Repeat for every server, using the listed peer IPs. Only WireGuard UDP needs these rules; private tests and service traffic use the encrypted tunnel.
firewallRules.requiredHint: Allow the listed traffic before continuing. Blocked connections prevent the network from working.
firewallRules.nativeDescription: Existing private networks, including Hetzner vSwitch, still need firewall access. Allow these TCP and UDP connections between the selected private IPs.
firewallRules.nativeFailedHint: Check the private routes, selected interfaces, and TCP/UDP rules in host and provider firewalls before retrying.
firewallRules.nativeScopeHint: These rules allow connectivity checks. Add the private service ports required by your workloads separately.
firewallRules.nativeFirewallHint: Configure host and provider firewalls for the private interface. OpenShip checks this network without changing its firewall rules.
firewallRules.confirmManaged: I’ve allowed the listed UDP traffic in the provider firewalls and routers between these servers.
firewallRules.confirmNative: I’ve allowed the listed TCP/UDP traffic in the host and provider firewalls for these private addresses.
firewallRules.confirmHint: OpenShip will verify connectivity after you continue.
firewallRules.nativeReturnHint: Stateful firewalls allow replies automatically. The template also includes reply rules for stateless firewalls, using the same private peer IPs.
